brain.name: Brain
brain.blurb: Computer and AI agent that plans the work and drives everything else.

eyes.name: Eyes
eyes.blurb: Cameras so Phil can see LEDs, switch presses and wiring without a person looking.

hands.name: Hands
hands.blurb: Firmware programmers, radios and I/O boards. The programmers stay attached, so Phil can reprogram devices on the fly.

maker.name: Switch tester
maker.blurb: A 3D printer used as a robot finger: it moves to a light switch and presses it, over and over, to test it.

test.name: Under test
test.blurb: Test fixtures and the lighting-control devices being tested.

power.name: Power
power.blurb: Mains power, wiring and the cart itself.

photos.title: The whole cart
photos.caption: Front view of Phil, top shelf to casters.

items.name: Overhead camera arm
items.desc: Articulating "magic arm" (orange locking knobs) clamped to the top shelf, holding small USB cameras that look down over the desk and the switch-testing printer.

items.name: Center camera arm
items.desc: Second magic arm hanging from the shelf with two webcams. Gives Phil a view of the work surface and the switch on the printer bed.

items.name: Monitor running Claude
items.desc: Acer monitor showing the Claude desktop app on macOS. The open sessions are Phil's projects (EnOcean 902 MHz module, CC1310 sniffer, BLE switch OTA from phone, LabJack status, unattended-loop runs).

items.name: Keyboard and mouse
items.desc: For people to step in. Day to day, Phil works through the computer without them.

items.name: Powered USB hub
items.desc: Multi-port hub with yellow-tagged cables. Fans the computer out to the programmers, cameras and boards on the shelves below.

items.name: Red board on black case
items.desc: A red development board sitting on a black enclosure, connected by USB. Not labeled in the photo; confirm what it is.

items.name: Switch-pressing 3D printer
items.desc: Creality 3D printer (looks like an Ender-3 V3 series) used only to test light switches. Phil moves the print head onto the switch mounted on the bed to press it, the same way every time.

items.name: Switch-test camera
items.desc: Webcam on a short arm aimed at the printer bed so Phil can watch each switch press and see the result.

items.name: Mac mini
items.desc: Phil's computer. Runs Claude Code and every tool that talks to the hardware.

items.name: Tethered phone
items.desc: Smartphone plugged in over USB, used to test phone apps such as BLE switch updates sent from a phone.

items.name: Firmware programmer panel
items.desc: Pegboard of firmware programmers and radio tools. They stay attached to the devices, so Phil can reprogram them on the fly between tests. See the close-up photo, items 19 to 24.

items.name: Close-up camera
items.desc: Webcam on a magic arm pointed at the boards so Phil can read LEDs and check status.

items.name: Lighting test panel
items.desc: Pegboard test fixture: an Arduino-driven breadboard wired to mains and 0-10 V lighting circuits, with firmware programmers attached so the devices can be reprogrammed during a test. See the close-up, items 27 to 33.

items.name: Surge strip "A-17"
items.desc: Prime surge-protected power strip with a lighted switch. Feeds the test panels.

items.name: Gateway panel
items.desc: Bottom pegboard with a wireless lighting gateway (red ring light), a 0-10 V controller and a breadboard.

items.name: Arduino "EBL-CL-0001"
items.desc: Small red Arduino-style board on a breadboard, labeled arduino EBL-CL-0001. Switches or simulates inputs for the gateway panel.

items.name: Main power cord
items.desc: White cord that powers the whole cart. In these photos the plug is lying on the floor, not in the wall.

items.name: Locking casters
items.desc: Chrome wire shelving rack on locking wheels, so Phil can be rolled to wherever the work is.

photos.title: Test shelves up close
photos.caption: Looking down at the programmer panel, the lighting test panel and the gateway panel.

items.name: SEGGER J-Link EDU
items.desc: Labeled "J-Link-EDU Programmer". Debug probe for flashing and debugging ARM microcontrollers. Stays attached so Phil can reflash firmware on the fly.

items.name: EnOcean Bridge
items.desc: Black USB device labeled "EnOcean Bridge". Lets the computer send and receive EnOcean wireless telegrams.

items.name: TI CC1310 radio
items.desc: Small board with a green LED, labeled TI CC1310. Sub-GHz radio used as a sniffer to capture 902 MHz traffic.

items.name: ILLUMRA module
items.desc: White ILLUMRA lighting-control module (an EnOcean-based product line) wired into the test circuits.

items.name: ST-LINK programmer
items.desc: White stick with the ST logo and a red LED. Programs and debugs STM32 microcontrollers. Stays attached so Phil can reflash firmware on the fly.

items.name: LabJack T4
items.desc: Red USB data-acquisition box. Gives Phil analog and digital I/O to measure voltages and toggle signals.

items.name: White round device
items.desc: Round white puck under the camera, similar in style to the gateway. Confirm whether it is a sensor or a second gateway.

items.name: Close-up camera
items.desc: Same camera as item 12, on its magic arm with an orange clamp knob.

items.name: Arduino Nano
items.desc: Blue Arduino Nano connected to the Mac by USB. The tester's controller: Phil sends it commands and it drives the channels next to it.

items.name: Driver channels
items.desc: Breadboard with four small three-pin parts and resistors, likely transistor or optocoupler stages that let the Nano switch the circuits under test.

items.name: Lever-nut connectors
items.desc: Orange WAGO-style lever connectors and yellow wire nuts join the panel's wires without soldering, so Phil can rewire quickly.

items.name: 0-10 V control wires
items.desc: Purple and gray pair printed "CONTROL 0-10V". The standard dimming signal used by commercial lighting.

items.name: Smart receptacle
items.desc: White outlet with an FCC ID label and screw terminals: a connected (wireless) receptacle being tested. A cord is plugged in as its load.

items.name: 4-button wireless switch
items.desc: Small white module with four button pads. Looks like an EnOcean PTM-style self-powered switch used as a wireless sender.

items.name: Black ring
items.desc: Round black core next to the wiring. Likely a ferrite or current-sense ring; confirm.

items.name: 0-10 V controller
items.desc: White box labeled "0-10v controller". Turns wireless commands into a 0-10 V dimming signal.

items.name: Gateway
items.desc: Round white wireless lighting gateway held down with cable ties. It shows a red ring light when powered.

items.name: Unplugged power cord
items.desc: The end of the main power cord (item 17) lying on the floor.
